newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says no need to drill ANWR for Sourdough oil.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says no need to drill ANWR for Sourdough oil.

text.p: The U.S. Interior Department said Monday it would not have to drill in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge in Alaska to see if oil under the refuge could be siphoned off through a neighboring field.
The adjacent field, called Sourdough, is on a state lease, where British Petroleum and Chevron last week announced a find that could hold 100 million barrels of oil.

"We do feel confident that if indeed there is drainage we can establish that without drilling within the boundaries of the refuge and we can protect taxpayers," Interior Department spokeswoman Stephanie Hanna said.

Hanna disputed comments by Sen. Frank Murkowski, a Republican from Alaska, who said the government might have to allow drilling in ANWR to determine if it should be owed any royalties on oil pumped out through the Sourdough field.

"Who does that oil belong to? The only way to find out is to find out if there's any oil on the other side," Murkowski told reporters after speaking at a National Ocean Industries Association meeting.
The Clinton administration has vehemently opposed opening any part of the refuge to oil and gas exploration.
Last week it repeated its concerns about drilling in the area when the companies announced the Sourdough find.

"We believe we will be able to work with the two oil companies and establish the amount of federal drainage," said Hanna, adding that they would use existing geophysical data and not disturb the surface of the refuge.
A BP spokesman said last week that while the company had wanted to drill in ANWR, "Sourdough is not a back-door approach to getting into ANWR."
